tests.label: After adding new SPT-3G D1 lensing, what survives when covariance-aware SH0ES, ACT/SPT primary-CMB stresses and the real T-POST PEER posterior are attacked together without invalid evidence stacking?
tests.summary: New SPT lensing strengthens active PEER and prefers the T-POST growth/lensing direction around f~0.09 conditionally. SH0ES-selected f=0.11883 remains SPT-compatible (~0.5σ), but ACT primary CMB still strongly penalizes that frozen high-f endpoint. Best current cross-probe compromise remains moderate f~0.05-0.08, with lensing pull toward 0.08-0.10.

SH0ES f=.1188275 ±.002: N=134, Zpred=.509, factor=2.28513. Moderate f=.0639±.005: factor=2.35123, equivalent descriptive ΔQ=-1.7099 vs ACT moderate +1.4847..+1.5387. ACT high-f +12.3773 vs SPT high-f equivalent -1.6528; SPT magnitude only 13.4% of ACT penalty.

tests.label: Does new SPT-3G D1 lensing remain compatible with or kill the covariance-aware SH0ES-selected high-f PEER branch?
tests.summary: SPT lensing does not kill the SH0ES-selected f≈0.1188 amplitude. In T-POST samples amplitude-matched to the exact SH0ES optimum, SPT is ~0.5σ away and gives a ~2.2-2.3× likelihood update versus the LCDM predictive distribution. ACT primary CMB still kills the frozen high-f endpoint.

tests.label: After adding new SPT-3G D1 lensing, do all materialized datasets and all still-live PEER/EDE variants survive, and which branch is strengthened or killed?
tests.summary: The 22-family canonical all-data matrix gains a favorable 23rd family: new SPT D1 lensing. No new robust PEER kill appears.
